digest.headline: Claude Fable 5.2 takes #1 on Artificial Analysis; Gemini 4 Carbon opens to developers; Meta ships Muse Ember
digest.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on November 9. Fable 5.2 is available everywhere at $8/$40 per million tokens, 20% cheaper than Fable 5.1 and up to 30% faster, and it now scores 65 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at max effort, six points ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon on the board. Mythos 5.2 stays limited to vetted cyber and life-sciences organizations. A day later Google opened Gemini 4 Carbon to paying developers and AI Ultra subscribers at an introductory $2/$10 that rises to $4/$20 after November 30; Carbon also tops CursorBench 4.0 at 60.4. Meta's Muse Ember is a small agent-execution model that matches Claude Haiku 5.5's AA score of 36 at about a third of the cost per task. Fireworks AI disclosed a second breach that reached billing data and, for some accounts, secrets, datasets and partial model weights. The MCP project proposed a file upload/download extension and moved to six-month spec releases. All three harnesses shipped: Claude Code 2.1.322 (Fable 5.2 as the default Fable model), Codex 0.167.2 (agent command center in 0.167.0), and Pi 1.5.2 (Pi 1.5.1 carried two breaking changes).

stories.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2: cheaper, faster, and #1 on Artificial Analysis
stories.dek: Released November 9. Fable 5.2 (`claude-fable-5-2`) is available on all platforms, including AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure, at $8 input and $40 output per million tokens, down from $10/$50, with a 1M-token context. Output is up to 30% faster than 5.1, and fast mode adds up to 2.5x at double the price. Mythos 5.2 is the same underlying model with fewer safeguards, limited to the Cyber and Life Sciences Verification Programs. Anthropic's own numbers put Fable 5.2 ahead of Opus 5.5 on FrontierCode 2.0 (49.1% vs 45.5% at xhigh), FrontierSWE v2 (69.9% vs 62.3%) and Terminal-Bench-Science. Independently, Artificial Analysis scores it 65 at max effort (#1) and 62 at high, and Cursor lists it at 60.0% on CursorBench 4.0. TechCrunch notes the system card reports both models suspect they're being evaluated more often than earlier models, and that Mythos 5.2 shows stronger covert capabilities on several evals.
stories.whyItMatters: The top of the AA index changed hands again within two weeks, and this time the leader is generally available. Anthropic still recommends Opus 5.5 as the everyday default, with Fable for the hardest open-ended work.

stories.title: Gemini 4 Carbon opens to paying developers and AI Ultra subscribers
stories.dek: On November 10 Google made Carbon available through the paid Gemini API in AI Studio, Gemini for business, Android Studio and CodeMender, and began rolling it out to AI Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, AI Mode in Search and Antigravity. Scientists can apply for six months of free access, and cyber defenders keep the Fairwind Program. The introductory price of $2 input and $10 output per million tokens ends November 30, after which it's $4/$20. Google says Carbon ranks #1 on CursorBench 4.0, Perplexity's WANDR and Zapier's AutomationBench at more than 2x lower cost per task than the next-best external model. Cursor's own leaderboard confirms the CursorBench lead: 60.4% at high effort, just ahead of Fable 5.2 Max at 60.0%.
stories.whyItMatters: Two weeks after a cyber-only debut, Carbon is now something you can actually call. If you want to test it cheaply, do it before the price doubles on November 30.

stories.title: Meta releases Muse Ember, a cheap small model for the repetitive steps in agent work
stories.dek: Released November 9 as `muse-ember-1.0` through the Meta Model API and Muse Code, Ember is the smallest model in the Muse line, with a 1M-token context and pricing of $0.10 input, $0.004 cached input and $0.50 output per million tokens. Meta built it to handle tool calls, coding subtasks, routing and extraction alongside a larger planner model. Artificial Analysis scores it 36 at max effort, level with Claude Haiku 5.5, at $0.14 per index task versus $0.41 for Haiku, the cheapest model AA has measured at that level. Unlike Meta's Muse Glimmer, Ember's weights aren't downloadable.
stories.whyItMatters: Small-model pricing is now a race on cached input, which dominates long agent loops. Ember is a candidate for subagent and routing work if you're already paying Haiku-class prices.

stories.title: Fireworks AI says a second breach reached billing data, secrets, datasets and partial model weights
stories.dek: In a November 9 update to its October security bulletin, Fireworks says a third-party cloud provider hosting its R&D machines was compromised on October 23, and an attacker used that access on October 24 to run an unauthorized workload on Fireworks development machines. Accessed data included resource metadata, billing details such as addresses, invoices and credit usage, and, for a limited set of accounts, stored secrets, datasets and incomplete model weights. Fireworks says its Inference, Training SDK and Nexus products are zero data retention by default and weren't affected, and that card numbers aren't stored. The investigation is ongoing and affected customers are being notified directly.
stories.whyItMatters: Inference platforms hold API keys, fine-tuning data and unreleased weights in one place. If you've stored secrets or uploaded datasets to Fireworks, rotate the keys now rather than waiting for a notification.

stories.title: MCP drafts a file upload/download extension and moves to six-month spec releases
stories.dek: On November 10 the File Uploads Working Group published an experimental extension, `io.modelcontextprotocol/files`, that moves files between clients and tools without passing the bytes through the model. Servers mark file arguments with `x-mcp-file`; small files go inline, while larger ones get an `upload_required` result with an HTTPS target, and downloads come back as targets in `_meta` with optional SHA-256 checks. There's no reference implementation yet, and the group aims to make it stable by year end. A day later the project announced specs will ship every six months, on the last Tuesday of March and September, with the next one targeted for March 30, 2027.
stories.whyItMatters: Getting files in and out of tools is one of the biggest practical gaps in MCP today. A fixed release calendar also means SDK betas arrive 1.5 months before each spec, so server authors know when to test.

stories.title: Nvidia reportedly tightens overseas cloud GPU rentals to Chinese customers
stories.dek: Tom's Hardware reports that Nvidia is requiring overseas cloud partners to reserve at least 51% of their capacity for non-Chinese customers, closing a route Chinese firms have used to rent restricted GPUs abroad. The same report says black-market prices for B300 server racks in China have climbed to about $2.8 million. Nvidia's terms haven't been published, so details rest on the report.
stories.whyItMatters: Renting compute offshore has been the main workaround for export limits. Tighter rental quotas push Chinese labs further toward domestic chips, which matters for how fast open-weights competitors from China can keep up.

modelsMeta.note: Board rebuilt October 5. Since the last refresh, Artificial Analysis moved to Intelligence Index v4.3 and CursorBench to 4.0, both on much lower absolute scales (Claude Opus 5 went from 61 to 51 on AA). So every row now uses the current versions; the old numbers aren't comparable. New this cycle: Claude Opus 5.5 (the new AA #1 at 58), Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6.1 Sol, and Grok 4.7. Grok 4.6's AA score is derived from AA's statement that Grok 4.7 scored +2 over it. DeepSWE figures come from BenchLM's aggregation (last updated Sep 1), plus Opus 5.5's 74.2 from BenchLM's head-to-head. Gemini 4 Argon is not listed yet because it has no independent scores. Older models no longer near the frontier (Opus 4.8, Grok 4.5, Qwen3.8-Max, Kimi K3, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Pro, DeepSeek V4 Flash) were dropped because they lack v4.3 / CursorBench 4.0 scores. October 7: added Mistral Large 4 (AA 38, research preview Oct 6); it has no CursorBench 4.0 or DeepSWE score yet. Reflection's Beam is not listed because it has only self-reported scores. October 8: added Claude Haiku 5.5 (AA 43 at max effort, released Oct 7); it has no CursorBench 4.0 or DeepSWE score yet. October 24: added Muse Wonder Full (AA 56) and Muse Wonder (AA 52), both released Oct 12; Kimi K3.1 Pro (AA 55, Oct 23); and Gemini 4 Argon (AA 53, generally available Oct 13). Argon was previously held back for lacking independent scores. None of them has a CursorBench 4.0 or BenchLM DeepSWE score yet (BenchLM CursorBench updated Oct 23; DeepSWE still Sep 1). Google's self-reported DeepSWE 77.9% for Argon is not listed because it was run on a different harness. October 27: added GPT-6.1 Terra (AA 45 at xhigh effort, released Oct 26); it has no CursorBench 4.0 or DeepSWE score yet. November 2: AA column rebased to Intelligence Index v5.0 (launched Oct 27; ~60% private test sets, new FrontierCode 2.0 and Terminal-Bench-Science, GDPval-AA, SciCode and AA-LCR removed). v5 scores aren't comparable with v4.3, so every AA value was replaced with its current v5 score at the highest reasoning setting AA lists (e.g. Argon 53 → 50, Sonnet 5.5 56 → 54, Muse Wonder 52 → 43; Terra is now listed at max, 51, instead of xhigh). CursorBench and DeepSWE values are unchanged. Added Gemini 4 Carbon (AA 59, the new #1, announced Oct 28, limited access); no CursorBench 4.0 or DeepSWE score yet. Dropped Claude Opus 5, Claude Fable 5, GPT-5.6 Sol and Grok 4.6: AA marks them deprecated with no v5 score. November 11: added Claude Fable 5.2 (AA 65 at max, the new #1, released Nov 9; CursorBench 4.0 60.0 at Max) and Muse Ember (AA 36 at max, released Nov 9). Filled newly listed CursorBench 4.0 scores at each model's highest listed effort: Gemini 4 Carbon 60.4 (High), Gemini 4 Argon 52.9 (High), Muse Wonder 50.4 (Max), Claude Haiku 5.5 48.4 (Max). Claude Mythos 5.2 (Nov 9) is not listed: it is restricted to vetted organizations and has no independent scores. BenchLM's DeepSWE is still dated Sep 1, so no new DeepSWE values. Existing AA values were not re-checked; AA's current pages may differ by a point.

harness.notes: 2.1.322 (Nov 10) enables fast mode on Vertex AI in the global, us and eu regions, falling back to standard speed if Vertex refuses it. 2.1.321 (Nov 9) adds Claude Fable 5.2 (`claude-fable-5-2`) as the default Fable model, with 1M context and $8/$40 pricing, plus `--settings <file>` for `claude remote-control`. 2.1.319 (Nov 6) adds terminal support for MCP tasks (opt out with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MCP_TASK_BACKGROUND`), a `permissions.denyInsteadOfPrompting` setting, `/claude-api latency-optimize`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEATURE_FLAGS`. 2.1.318 (Nov 4) adds `loginExpiresAt` to `claude auth status` and a "No repository" option for cloud sessions. 2.1.317 (Nov 3) warns in `/schedule` when a new cloud task gets connectors you didn't ask for, and asks before a web or shell tool call sends your account email. Reminder: Opus 4.8 fast mode is removed November 30.

0.167.2 sends tool updates incrementally by default on Google Cloud Vertex AI (`incremental_tools_legacy_gcp` under `[features]` controls it). 0.167.0 (Nov 6) is the big one: an agent command center via `codex agents --no-daemon` with unread markers, switching between connected backends from the session picker without losing drafts, local image previews while composing, a Vertex AI setup wizard behind `gcp_setup_wizard`, opt-in system proxy settings in `/experimental`, and expandable patch details during approval prompts. Fixes keep saved chats visible after switching providers, make `Ctrl+L` clear the screen with history still on `Ctrl+T`, and make compaction account for output from failed responses.

1.5.2 offers Continue, Fork or Cancel when a session's original folder is gone, and fixes duplicate copies from `/import`. 1.5.1 (Nov 9) has two breaking changes: custom `GrepOperations.readFile` callbacks are no longer called for context lines (the field is deprecated), and OpenAI-compatible models omit an empty `tools` array once tools are disabled; proxies that need it can set `compat.requiresToolsWithToolHistory: true`. It also adds `pi auth login`/`logout` from the shell, idle prompt-cache warming for up to 30 minutes (now the default `cacheWarming` mode), incremental Anthropic message threads, more Mermaid chart types, and Claude Fable 5.2; the default Anthropic model is now Claude Opus 5.5. Grep `glob` patterns now resolve relative to `path`.

extensions.name: MCP Files extension (io.modelcontextprotocol/files)
extensions.blurb: A draft, optional extension for spec 2026-07-28 and later that lets tools take and return files without routing bytes through the model. The client sends file metadata first so the server can check permissions and quota, then uploads out of band over HTTPS. Credentials are only sent to the MCP server's own origin, and redirects are refused. No reference implementation yet; feedback goes to the `experimental-ext-file-uploads` repo.

extensions.name: InfrOS MCP server
extensions.blurb: Launched in preview for eligible customers on November 9. Your assistant can gather requirements, compare architecture proposals with projected monthly costs, and pull generated Terraform into your workspace. It never writes to your repos or opens PRs, OAuth scopes separate read, edit, credit-spending and admin access, and design runs use organization credits.

extensions.name: MCP 2027-03-30 release calendar
extensions.blurb: MCP specs now ship every six months, on the last Tuesday of March and September, starting with 2027-03-30. Soft freeze lands 2.5 months before release, Tier 1 SDK betas 1.5 months before, and hard freeze a month before. Existing clients and servers don't need changes; the betas are your window to test against the new spec early.

tips.title: Try Fable 5.2 at high effort before reaching for max
tips.body: Anthropic says Fable 5.2 at high effort scores about the same as Opus 5.5 at max on FrontierCode 2.0 for roughly half the cost per task, and matches Opus 5.5's top WANDR score at medium for about 40% of the cost. Artificial Analysis shows the same shape: 62 at high versus 65 at max. Medium is the default in Claude Code. Anthropic's own guidance is to keep Opus 5.5 as the daily driver and use Fable as an advisor or orchestrator for the hardest problems.

tips.title: Keep prompt caches warm between agent runs
tips.body: Pi 1.5.1 adds idle prompt-cache warming, which keeps eligible caches warm for up to 30 minutes between runs, and makes it the default `cacheWarming` mode instead of `"streaming"`. If you work in bursts with pauses to review diffs, this avoids paying full input price to rebuild a long context on your next prompt. Combined with cheap cached input like Muse Ember's $0.004 per million tokens, cache hit rate is now one of the biggest levers on agent cost.

tips.title: Check what connectors your scheduled cloud tasks get
tips.body: Claude Code 2.1.317 warns in `/schedule` when a new cloud scheduled task is given connectors you didn't ask for, and asks before a web or shell tool call sends your account email. Unattended tasks are where an over-broad connector does the most damage, so review the connector list each time you create one and remove anything the task doesn't need.
